modules.name: Lift traffic sizing and zoning by use
modules.design_question: How many lifts, of what size and speed, in how many rises, serve each use at acceptable service, and how much total core area (passenger plus service) results?
modules.effort: L: about 14-16 person-days for v1 (general-analysis RTT with express term and kinematics 5, service-lift layer 3, population templates 3, rise diagram and gauges 3, unit tests 2). SimPy dispatch is roadmap, 15+ more.
inputs: Layer 0: area per storey by program tag; unit counts by bedroom type; hotel room count
Layer 0: floor-to-floor heights (unequal allowed), storey count, main-lobby and below-grade transit levels
Core footprint and shaft availability from the massing/core module
User presets: density or persons per unit and room, utilisation, car library entry, speed, acceleration, jerk, door times, control type, traffic profile
User entries: transit mode share, station peak flow, escalator or shuttle capacity
Service-lift presets: firefighter, stretcher, goods, parking lifts
outputs: LiftGroupSpec[] (rise, floors served, express floors, cars, rated load, speed, traffic profile)
VTPerformance {RTT, HC5 %, interval per group; AWT and ATTD badged 'simulation not performed'}
CoreAreaByLevel {passenger shafts, service and firefighter shafts, lobbies, pits and overruns} reported separately and as total
NetToGross per typical level, computed from total core
RegulatoryFlags {seismic, single-run rise, sway, stack effect, regulator acceptance}

parameters.name: Population basis by use
parameters.unit: m2 NIA per person; persons per unit; persons per room
parameters.relationship: Office: area / density x utilisation. Residential and hotel: persons per unit (1.5 to 4.0 by bedrooms) or per room. More people add cars and shafts. Default 1 per 10 m2 is a team assumption; 1 per 8 is a London buffer.

parameters.name: Floors per rise (zone height)
parameters.relationship: More floors per rise adds probable stops and flight time, lengthening round-trip time and cutting capacity per car; more rises cut core area per rise but add transfer floors and limit interfloor travel.

parameters.name: Rated speed, acceleration and jerk
parameters.relationship: Faster cars shorten flight time, so taller rises use higher speeds to hold similar round-trip times; on long express runs the speed profile (acceleration, jerk) sets the real run time. Gains shrink when door and loading time dominate.

parameters.name: Car rated load and platform area
parameters.relationship: Larger cars carry more per trip, raising capacity per shaft but lengthening loading and enlarging the shaft. EN 81 pairs (1600 kg/21 persons) are placeholders; Canadian cars follow CSA B44 load-to-platform rules. Table values not retrieved.

parameters.name: Control type (collective vs destination)
parameters.relationship: Destination control groups passengers by floor, cutting stops and non-coincident stops; its benefit must be shown by simulation, so v1 reports calculation results only.

parameters.name: Use zoning (separate groups by use)
parameters.relationship: Separate groups for basement, residential, hotel, office and public shuttles keep mixed traffic out of the main group, protecting its handling capacity at the cost of more shafts.

parameters.name: Lowest terminal (below-grade transit entrance)
parameters.relationship: A second terminal below the main lobby adds a long first flight and extra stops to every round trip; a dedicated group or escalators keeps this traffic off the main group (22 Bishopsgate main lifts skipped basements).

parameters.name: Utilisation factor (share of floor population present at peak)
parameters.relationship: Scales design population; 22 Bishopsgate used 80%, so a lower factor trims lifts but risks under-provision if tenants over-occupy.

parameters.name: Express-zone run (unserved floors below a rise)
parameters.relationship: Floors a rise skips below its first served floor add twice the express run time to every round trip, so upper rises of a 244-305 m tower need higher speed or more cars. The classic formula omits this term.

parameters.name: Average car load P
parameters.relationship: P is the average passengers per trip, about 80% of capacity in hand estimates and calculated in general analysis. Higher P raises HC5 per car but lengthens loading time; rated capacity must not be used as P.

parameters.name: Traffic profile (up-peak, two-way, lunch)
parameters.relationship: Each profile changes which stops and directions count, so a gauge is valid only for its profile. v1 computes up-peak; two-way and lunch templates for residential, hotel and mixed-use stacking are roadmap.

parameters.name: Service and firefighter lifts
parameters.relationship: Firefighter, stretcher, goods and parking lifts add shafts, lobbies, pits and overruns that passenger counts omit; one 22 Bishopsgate goods lift needed 7,400 kg special operation. Counts are editable presets by GFA and use.

parameters.name: Transit mode share and station peak flow
parameters.relationship: User-entered mode share and station flow set demand at the below-grade terminal; escalator or shuttle capacity then sizes a separate group so these riders stay off the main group. No TransLink figures sourced.

parameters.name: Seismic, wind, rope-length and stack-effect constraints
parameters.relationship: BC requires CSA B44-16; seismic provisions, post-earthquake lift availability, rope and building sway in high wind, maximum single-run rise and stack-effect door forces can cap rise height and speed. All flags are unverified.

metrics.name: Up-peak 5-minute handling capacity (office)
metrics.basis: Applicability: institutional target (UQ DS-11, 13%, Australia) and worked example (Peters, 12%, UK practice). Not a Canadian code limit. Profile: up-peak.
metrics.method: HC5 = 300 x P x N / RTT / population x 100, P = average car load

metrics.name: Up-peak average interval (office)
metrics.basis: Applicability: institutional (UQ: under 30 s) and worked example (Peters: 30 s). Profile: up-peak.

metrics.name: Up-peak average waiting time (office, all floors served)
metrics.bad: red: AWT > 30, or AWT > 25 with ATTD > 80; amber: 25 < AWT <= 30 with ATTD <= 80
metrics.basis: Applicability: UK speculative-office guidance (BCO 2014) quoted second-hand by Stopes; later BCO editions unchecked, superseded-edition check pending. v1 badge: simulation not performed; estimate AWT = interval / 2.
metrics.method: v1: AWT = interval / 2; roadmap: Monte Carlo simulation

metrics.name: Up-peak average time to destination (office)
metrics.bad: red: ATTD > 110, or ATTD > 90 with AWT >= 25; amber: 90 < ATTD <= 110 with AWT < 25
metrics.basis: Applicability: UK guidance (BCO 2014) quoted by Stopes; superseded-edition check pending. The project itself targeted 30 s and 80 s. v1 badge: simulation not performed.
metrics.method: Roadmap: simulated waiting plus ride time

metrics.name: Residential two-way handling capacity and interval
metrics.basis: Applicability: project example (Arup, 74-level Sydney tower, CIBSE Guide D values) and institutional (UQ: 8%, under 40 s). Profile: two-way. v1 badge: not computed until the two-way template is validated.

metrics.name: Hotel, cultural, observation and public-use traffic criteria
metrics.basis: No sourced criteria found; editable preset shown as a team assumption with its traffic profile named.

metrics.name: Floors per single-deck rise
metrics.basis: Applicability: UK practice (CIBSE Guide D as cited by Peters). Fast tall residential rises of 21-28 floors in the Arup design show this is a review flag, not a ban.

metrics.name: Net-to-gross area ratio (NIA/GIA), typical floor
metrics.basis: Applicability: UK practitioner statement (Stopes); Canadian measurement conventions differ. Computed from total core (passenger plus service, firefighter, lobbies), not passenger shafts only.
metrics.method: NIA / GIA after subtracting total core, lobbies and shafts

metrics.name: Passenger-shaft share of floor plate by level
metrics.good: lowest option that meets all gauges above
metrics.basis: Report-only comparison; no sourced threshold. Peters counts passenger shafts only, excluding goods and firefighting lifts and lobbies.
metrics.method: sum of passenger shaft footprints at level / floor plate area

metrics.name: Total lift core area vs passenger-only area
metrics.bad: total omitted or equal to passenger-only
metrics.basis: Passenger-only figures flatter net-to-gross; total adds firefighter, stretcher, goods and parking lifts, lobbies, pits and overruns from presets.
metrics.method: passenger shafts + service shafts + lobbies + pits and overruns

metrics.name: Stretcher-capable car provided
metrics.good: green: at least one car takes a 2010 x 610 mm stretcher
metrics.basis: Applicability: code text of VBBL 2007 (3.5.4.1); the 2024 checklist lists the clause but dimensions are unread. Re-check VBBL 2025.

metrics.name: Transit-level peak demand vs shuttle or escalator capacity
metrics.basis: No sourced flows or escalator capacity; the user enters station peak flow and mode share.
metrics.method: tower population at the level x mode share vs capacity

modules.method: 1) Population per level: area / density x utilisation (office); persons per unit or room (residential, hotel). 2) Group floors into rises by use and height; add a group for transit levels. 3) Per rise compute RTT by general analysis: kinematic flight times per floor interval (unequal heights), express-zone run 2 x tx, stops S and reversal floor H from floor populations, door and transfer times, P = average car load. The classic form 2H*tv + (S+1)*ts + 2P*tp is the equal-floor case (formula from standard texts, not P11-S23). 4) HC5 = 300 x P x N / RTT / population; interval = RTT / N; pick the smallest N meeting the bands. 5) Core area = passenger plus service, firefighter and stretcher lifts, lobbies, pits, overruns, reported separately and in total. 6) Unit-test against the Peters worked example and Arup rises (levels 4-25, 26-46, 47-74 at 3.5, 5.0, 6.0 m/s) before any gauge shows pass/fail.
visualization: Rise diagram: storeys on the vertical axis, one column per rise, solid = served, hatched = express, T = transfer floor (style of P11-S23 Fig. 1), beside a 3D tower section
Gauge bars for HC5 and interval with green, amber and red bands, a source badge and the traffic-profile label; AWT and ATTD gauges greyed 'simulation not performed'
Stacked core plans at ground, mid and top levels: passenger shafts, service lifts and lobbies in separate colours
Group specification table (cars, rating, speed, floors served, code family of the car preset)
modules.human_judgment: Tenant density and utilisation, acceptable waiting for each use, whether transfers are acceptable, public-use traffic assumptions, and final lift selection and simulation by a vertical-transportation consultant.
modules.limits: v1 is an up-peak calculation only; two-way, lunch, down-peak and SimPy dispatch are roadmap. Guidance is UK/Australian, not Canadian code. Guide D text is paywalled. Early estimate, not certification.

modules.name: Lift strategy comparator: sky lobby, double-deck, destination control
modules.design_question: Which lift strategy (single-deck rises, sky lobby with shuttles, then double-deck and destination control) minimises total core area while keeping accessible, secure public-use floors high in the tower?
modules.effort: M: about 5 person-days for the single-deck and sky-lobby comparison on top of P11-M01; double-deck and destination dispatch are roadmap (15+ person-days with validation)
inputs: LiftGroupSpec[] and VTPerformance from P11-M01
Layer 0: storey heights (equal or varied) and floor-use tags, including public or cultural floors high in the tower
Candidate sky-lobby and transfer floors
Structural core constraints from the structure module
User switches: direct-travel preference, public sky-room intent, security separation for public floors
outputs: StrategyOptionTable {total core m2, shafts at ground, transfers per typical trip, floor-height constraints}
SelectedStrategy flag for P11-M03 (machine rooms, overruns) and P11-M05 (firefighter elevator access)
FirefighterLiftReach {changes, run time, 'requires AHJ agreement' tag}

parameters.name: Strategy type
parameters.relationship: Double-deck halves possible stops and puts two cabs per shaft; sky lobbies drop express zones from upper rises, usually saving more core than the shuttles add. Two independent cars per shaft equal double-deck for core space. v1 compares single-deck and sky lobby.

parameters.name: Floor-to-floor height uniformity
parameters.relationship: Double-deck cabs serve adjacent floors together, so every served floor needs equal height; double-height public floors then need escalators, separate lifts or adjustable-spacing cabs (22 Bishopsgate kept an amenity level off its double-deck groups).

parameters.name: Transfers per journey (design-intent switch)
parameters.relationship: Sky lobbies force two-lift trips; London tenants demanded direct travel, steering 22 Bishopsgate to double-deck. VTC public floors high in the tower may favour sky lobbies as public rooms, so this is a switch, not a pass/fail.

parameters.name: Sky-lobby position and shuttle design
parameters.relationship: A top-down shuttle to the top of one local group is core-efficient but sends some riders up then down; shuttling to the lowest floor of each local group is intuitive but needs more core. Double-deck shuttles need a double-deck sky lobby.

parameters.name: Firefighter elevator continuity and run time
parameters.relationship: One firefighter elevator must reach every above-grade floor served with at most one change and a 60 s run to the top (VBBL 2007 text), so zoning, sky lobbies and 300 m height constrain it. London shared an upper deck by building-control agreement.

parameters.name: Magnet floors (observation, restaurant, public cultural)
parameters.relationship: These concentrate trips on a few floors; dedicated high-speed shuttles (8.0 m/s at 22 Bishopsgate) keep them off the main groups but add shafts.

parameters.name: Destination control
parameters.relationship: Raises up-peak capacity and cuts non-coincident stops in double-deck groups; confirm by simulation where average waiting time must not exceed 80% of the nominated interval (UQ rule). Manufacturer gains are unverified.

parameters.name: Public and observation access separation
parameters.relationship: Public and observation visitors need security separation from tenant groups; dedicated shuttles or separate sky-lobby entrances add shafts but protect tenant lifts and support the VTC aim of public uses extending up the tower.

parameters.name: Regulator acceptance for novel systems
parameters.relationship: Double-deck, multi-car and ropeless options may need acceptance by Technical Safety BC under the Elevating Devices Safety Regulation; its page is silent on them, so the tool flags 'regulator acceptance required' until confirmed.

parameters.name: Evacuation-lift option
parameters.relationship: Occupant-evacuation lifts could shorten total evacuation of a 250-300 m tower; CIBSE Guide D chapter 6 covers them, but no Canadian requirement was retrieved. Linked to P11-M08 evacuation time; status unresolved.

metrics.name: Total core shaft area vs single-deck baseline at equal service
metrics.good: lower than baseline with all P11-M01 bands green or amber
metrics.bad: saving achieved only by a red P11-M01 band
metrics.basis: No universal saving percentage found; Peters reports option-specific core charts only. Uses total core, not passenger shafts only.
metrics.method: sum of total core footprints per option

metrics.name: Double-deck floor-height uniformity
metrics.good: green: all stopped floors equal height
metrics.bad: red: any stopped floor differs without an adjustable-spacing cab
metrics.basis: Applicability: engineering principle stated by Peters (UK practice); all floors must be equal height for double-deck cabs.
metrics.method: compare storey heights at served floors

metrics.name: Destination-control waiting time vs nominated interval
metrics.basis: Applicability: institutional (UQ DS-11, Australia), not code. v1 badge: simulation not performed; roadmap item.
metrics.method: Roadmap: simulated average waiting time / nominated interval

metrics.name: Transfers per typical trip (design-intent switch)
metrics.good: no pass/fail: direct (0) or one transfer to a public sky room, chosen by the team
metrics.basis: Direct travel is a London speculative-office criterion (Stopes); Vancouver market and VTC jury preference are unsourced.
metrics.method: count lift changes on the path lobby to floor

metrics.name: Firefighter elevator changes to reach any floor
metrics.basis: Edition stamp VBBL 2007; value in BCBC 2024 and VBBL 2025 unread, so the current edition shows 'not assessed'. Add 'requires AHJ agreement' when combined with a passenger double-deck.
metrics.method: graph search on shaft and lobby connectivity

metrics.name: Firefighter elevator run time to top served floor
metrics.basis: VBBL 2007 text; current edition unread. At 244-305 m this sets a minimum rated speed for the firefighter shaft or a change floor.
metrics.method: run time from the speed profile over the distance from the firefighter entrance level

metrics.name: Non-coincident stop share (double-deck figure of merit)
metrics.basis: Defined by Peters as the percentage of stops coincident for both cabs; no limit stated. Roadmap with double-deck.
metrics.method: Monte Carlo with odd/even floor restriction (roadmap)

modules.method: For each option, re-run P11-M01 using total core. Single-deck: N rises by floors per rise. Sky lobby: shuttle group (express flight, few stops) plus local groups, transfer floors flagged, express term included. Rank options by total core area subject to P11-M01 bands not red. Compute transfers per journey (shown as a design-intent switch), firefighter-elevator changes and run time, and public-floor access. Double-deck (stops roughly halved by odd/even restriction) and destination dispatch are roadmap: their round-trip formulas were not retrieved, so implement from the worked cases in P11-S23 and validate before showing pass/fail.
visualization: Side-by-side rise diagrams per option with transfer floors marked (style of P11-S23 Figs 1, 5, 7, 9)
Stacked bar of total core shaft area by level for each option
Badge row (floor-height equality, firefighter reach and run time, regulator acceptance) linked to source
Sky-lobby floors drawn on the 3D tower with an annotation for public-room potential
modules.human_judgment: Trade-off between core efficiency, direct travel and public-room potential; whether transfers are acceptable for public and cultural users; security separation; vendor-neutral choice among double-deck and multi-car systems; authority agreement for a shared firefighter lift.
modules.limits: Double-deck and shuttle formulas not retrieved. Manufacturer gains for destination dispatch (25-30%, P11-S33) are unverified marketing figures. No Canadian market or regulator precedent found for sky-lobby transfers.

modules.name: Mechanical floors, plant space and risers
modules.design_question: How many plant floors, where, and how much plant, electrical and riser area does the tower need, and how do they shape the silhouette and public-facing floors?
inputs: Layer 0: tower height, storey heights, program areas by tag (mechanical tag = existing plant)
Plant capacities and electrical demand from P11-M04
Lift overrun, pit and machine-room needs from P11-M01 and P11-M02
Outrigger or transfer floors from the structure module
User presets: hydronic equipment pressure rating, air-handling reach, area per kW
outputs: PlantFloorSchedule {level, function, area m2, floor height} with a minimum-to-maximum floor count
DomesticWaterZoneTable {zone, level range, static head kPa, PRV station}
RiserAllocation {riser type, area per level, core or perimeter}
PlantShare (information only) and LouvreZones for the facade module

parameters.name: Domestic-water static head and PRV stations
parameters.relationship: Static head is 9.81 kPa per m. Where static pressure may exceed 550 kPa a pressure-reducing valve is required (BC Plumbing Code 6.3.3.(1)); designers use PRV stations per zone, not plant floors. Vancouver Book II is NPC 2020-based; text unread.

parameters.name: Hydronic pressure break (equipment rating)
parameters.relationship: Chilled and heating water static head also rises 9.81 kPa per m; where it exceeds the rating of heat exchangers, chillers or coils, a heat-exchanger break at a plant floor is needed. The rating is an editable team preset.

parameters.name: Air-handling reach and riser congestion
parameters.relationship: Supply and return duct reach, shaft area and damper count limit how many floors one plant floor can serve; shorter reach adds plant floors and louvred bands on the facade. Reach is an editable preset.

parameters.name: Plant-floor frequency (sanity range)
parameters.relationship: A weak tertiary rule of thumb gives about one plant floor per ten tenant floors; more frequent plant shortens risers but removes lettable or public floors and adds louvred bands. Used only as an information range.

parameters.name: Heavy plant location (generators, chillers)
parameters.relationship: Placing heavy plant at the top forces goods-lift capacity and riser routes to match; at 22 Bishopsgate, six smaller generators replaced five large ones, yet one goods lift still needed a 7,400 kg special operation.

parameters.name: Top-floor competition (plant vs public/observation)
parameters.relationship: Plant, viewing gallery and restaurant compete for top floors; at 22 Bishopsgate not every goods lift could serve every top floor.

parameters.name: Electrical room, substation and generator area
parameters.relationship: Peak electrical demand from P11-M04 sets transformer, switchroom and generator area through editable area-per-kW presets; heavy items drive goods-lift capacity and routes for plant replacement.

metrics.name: Plant floors as share of total floors
metrics.basis: Rule of thumb about 10% from a tertiary source (Wikipedia, citations needed); shown as a range until a CTBUH or engineering source is found.

metrics.name: Domestic-water static head per PRV zone
metrics.basis: Applicability: BC Plumbing Code 6.3.3.(1) per BCAB 1454 (1997 decision); Vancouver Book II is NPC 2020-based and unread. PRVs, not plant floors, handle this limit.

metrics.name: Hydronic static head vs equipment rating
metrics.basis: Equipment-rating preset is a team assumption; typical commercial ratings were not sourced.

metrics.name: Plant-floor count range
metrics.good: report minimum to maximum; user selects
metrics.bad: single value shown without a range
metrics.basis: Minimum from the larger of hydronic and air-handling needs; maximum from their sum; user-added floors on top. Range reflects unsourced presets.

metrics.name: Plant area as share of GFA
metrics.basis: No sourced percentage found; reported for comparison only.

metrics.name: Top-of-tower use conflict
metrics.good: plant and public or observation uses both accommodated with lift access
metrics.bad: plant displaces a public floor or lifts cannot reach
metrics.basis: Pattern observed at 22 Bishopsgate; a design check, not a code limit.
metrics.method: rule check on top five levels

modules.method: 1) Read height H and occupied floors. 2) Domestic water: zone height = 550 kPa / 9.81 kPa per m (about 56 m, unverified preset); PRV stations = ceil(H / zone height), placed in risers, not plant floors. 3) Hydronic: breaks = ceil(H x 9.81 / rating preset). 4) Air handling: floors served per plant floor from the reach preset. 5) Plant floors: minimum = larger of hydronic and air-handling need, maximum = their sum, plus user-added floors; snap to outrigger and sky-lobby floors. 6) Size area from P11-M04 capacities with area-per-kW presets; allocate risers and electrical rooms. 7) Report the floor count as a range and plant share as information only; flag top-floor conflicts.
visualization: Tower elevation strip: one cell per storey coloured by program tag, plant floors hatched, minimum and maximum plant options shown
Two pressure-zone bands: domestic PRV zones and hydronic breaks, each with its kPa legend
Plant share shown as an information range (7 to 26% observed) with source badge, no pass/fail colours
Typical riser stacking plan with shaft footprints
Conflict icons on the top floors
modules.human_judgment: Where plant sits relative to public and cultural floors and the skyline; facade louvre expression; coordination with structure, sky lobbies and fire engineer; MEP engineer sizing.
modules.limits: No sourced plant frequency, equipment pressure rating or area percentages by height. The 10% figure is a weak rule of thumb. Sizing uses editable presets; no duct or pipe hydraulic design.

modules.name: Low-carbon heating/cooling and GHG compliance screen (Vancouver by-law basis)
modules.design_question: Which low-carbon system keeps design energy and GHG intensity within Vancouver's Part 10 limits and rezoning policy, and what plant and electrical space does it need?
modules.effort: L: about 8-10 person-days including emission-factor tables, limit tables with edition stamps and EUI presets
inputs: Layer 0: floor area by program tag
Envelope and glazing ratio from the facade module
System selection (air-source or water-source heat pump, heat recovery, district energy, gas back-up)
Vancouver climate and design temperatures
District-energy availability flag (central business district; team assumption)
Governing basis switch: VBBL Part 10 limit table and edition (default VBBL 2019 preset, replace with VBBL 2025)
outputs: PlantCapacity (kW heating and cooling) for P11-M03
ElectricalDemand (kW) for electrical and substation space
LimitScreen {GHGI, TEUI, TEDI vs loaded Vancouver row; provincial Step Code level as reference only}

parameters.name: Emission factor by energy source
parameters.relationship: Operational GHG = energy x factor. Electricity and natural gas factors come from the City Energy Modelling Guidelines (presets 0.011 and 0.179, unverified); propane and oils (0.2155-0.2689) are provincial references. Electrifying heating cuts GHGI sharply.

parameters.name: District energy connection
parameters.relationship: A building on a Low Carbon Energy System gets relaxed TEUI and TEDI limits (Table 10.2.2.5.C, VBBL 2019 text); its emission factor is set by the authority with the utility. Downtown steam electrification is due 2027, so availability is an assumption.

parameters.name: Heat-pump COP and supply temperature
parameters.relationship: Thermodynamics: COP falls as the temperature lift (supply minus source) rises, so high-temperature heating or hot-water service lowers efficiency and raises electrical demand; COP values here are presets.

parameters.name: Vancouver GHGI, TEUI and TEDI limit set
parameters.relationship: Table 10.2.2.5.A1 (VBBL 2019 text): office TEUI 100, TEDI 20, GHGI 3.0; Group C over 6 storeys 120, 30, 3.0; hotel 140, 20, 4.0. Tighter limits shrink gas back-up and enlarge heat-pump and electrical space. VBBL 2025 table unread.

parameters.name: Rezoning energy policy
parameters.relationship: The tower is assumed to be a rezoning; the Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings (July 2023 version, summarised) asks for an energy and emissions report showing the design is on track for by-law limits expected at permit. Later versions unread.

parameters.name: Modelling basis
parameters.relationship: Part 10 compliance modelling follows NECB Part 8 and the City Energy Modelling Guidelines, so early estimates must be re-run in that framework for any real submission.

parameters.name: Provincial Step Code level (reference only)
parameters.relationship: BC Zero Carbon levels EL-1 to EL-4 and the Energy Step Code apply under BCBC, which the Province says does not apply in Vancouver. Levels are shown as a comparison, not as the compliance test.

metrics.name: Operational GHG intensity vs Vancouver limit
metrics.good: green: GHGI <= loaded limit (preset: office 3.0, hotel 4.0, Group C over 6 storeys 3.0)
metrics.basis: Applicability: Vancouver by-law Table 10.2.2.5.A1, VBBL 2019 text to 27 Feb 2025 (superseded). VBBL 2025 Part 10 unread; a 2022 council report summary says tighter 2025 limits were proposed.

parameters.name: Height of top-storey floor above grade
parameters.relationship: Subsection 3.2.6 applies above 18 m for Groups B and C; the NBC original adds 36 m for A, D, E, F (VBBL 2007 used 18 m for all). A 244-305 m tower triggers every measure, so the module records clause and edition only.

parameters.relationship: Taken from P11-M09; each group sets triggers and fire separations between major occupancies (3.1.3.1), so a mixed-use tower must satisfy the strictest combination.

parameters.name: Sprinkler status
parameters.relationship: Taken from P11-M09; the checklist cites sprinkler requirement and standard (3.2.2.18, 3.2.5.12, 3.2.5.14), standpipes (3.2.5.8-3.2.5.11) and fire pump (3.2.5.18).

parameters.name: Firefighter elevator layout
parameters.relationship: One firefighter elevator must reach every above-grade floor served with at most one change and a 60 s run to the top (VBBL 2007 text), in a protected shaft near stairs; this constrains zoned and sky-lobby lift schemes.

parameters.name: Stair smoke control by location
parameters.relationship: Stairs serving storeys above the lowest exit level need a bottom vent of 0.05 m2 per door, at least 1.8 m2. Stairs serving storeys below it, including transit-link levels, must hold contamination to 1% over 2 h.

parameters.name: Connected buildings (3.2.6.3)
parameters.relationship: The below-grade transit link may make the tower a connected building: measures must limit movement of contaminated air between buildings (VBBL 2007 text). The 2024 checklists omit 3.2.6.3 without explanation.

parameters.name: Alternative-solution path
parameters.relationship: Non-compliance needs an alternative solution achieving at least Division B performance (Appeal Board applies clause 1.2.1.1.(1)(b) of Division A); the register records rationale the VTC jury may weigh as a justified breach.

parameters.name: Protected zones and evacuation provisions
parameters.relationship: Protected zones (3.3.1.7) and any evacuation-elevator provision shape how people who cannot use stairs wait or leave; a refuge floor becomes an alternative-solution option tied to P11-M08 evacuation time.

modules.name: Egress sizing: occupant load, exits, stair width, travel distance
modules.design_question: How many occupants per storey, how many exit stairs of what width, what travel distances result, and how much core area do stairs take?
modules.effort: M: about 6 person-days including the travel-distance field
inputs: Layer 0: floor-plate polygons and area per storey by program tag
Stair and exit door locations from the core design
OccupancyMap and SprinklerStatus from P11-M09
Unit counts and bedroom counts for residential and hotel floors; core footprint and storey count from P11-M01

parameters.name: Occupant load factor per use
parameters.relationship: Load = area / Table 3.1.17.1 factor: office 9.30, mercantile 3.70 (basement, first storey) or 5.60, dining 1.20 (VBBL 2007); residential counts 2 persons per sleeping room. Denser uses widen exits and stairs.

parameters.name: Exit width per person
parameters.relationship: Width = load x 8 mm (stairs rise <= 180, run >= 280), 9.2 mm (steeper stairs, ramps over 1:8) or 6.1 mm (doors, corridors, gentle ramps). Each exit counts for at most half the required width, so two stairs each carry half.

parameters.name: Minimum clear width
parameters.relationship: Stairs serving more than two storeys above or one below the lowest exit level, and corridors, need at least 1100 mm (VBBL 2007 3.4.3.2.(8); Table 3.4.3.2.-A in 2024 unread). In a tall tower this minimum, not 8 mm per person, usually sets stair area.

parameters.name: Cumulative width
parameters.relationship: Required width need not accumulate in an exit serving floors one above the other (3.4.3.2.(4)) but does at interconnected floor spaces (3.4.3.2.(6)) and where exits converge (3.4.3.1.(2)). Sizing is per storey, so stairs do not widen down the tower.

parameters.name: Number and separation of exits
parameters.relationship: At least two exits per floor area (3.4.2.1); least distance between exits is half the maximum diagonal, with a 9 m rule for public-corridor floors (3.4.2.3). More stairs shorten travel but consume core and ground-floor frontage.

parameters.name: Travel distance limit
parameters.relationship: Limits sit in 3.4.2.5, measurement in 3.4.2.4, suites in 3.3.1.6. VBBL 2007: sprinklered 45 m, business and personal services 40 m, other 30 m, public corridor up to 105 m. The sprinkler switch from P11-M09 picks the limit.

parameters.name: Stair flight and handrail geometry
parameters.relationship: Flights are limited to 3.7 m rise except Group B Division 2 (3.4.6.3); stairs 1100 mm or wider need handrails on both sides (3.4.6.4 in 2007, 3.4.6.5 in the 2024 checklist); wider stairs add landing area and core size.

parameters.name: Emergency crossover access
parameters.relationship: The 2024 checklist lists crossover above 3 storeys above grade or 2 below (3.4.6.18); text unread. Do not confuse with stair re-entry doors (VBBL 2007 3.4.6.17, buildings over 6 storeys).

metrics.name: Stair width per person (standard stairs)
metrics.basis: Applicability: code, 3.4.3.2; same factor in VBBL 2007 text and the 2024 checklists. Re-check VBBL 2025.

metrics.name: Stair width per person (steeper stairs, ramps steeper than 1:8)
metrics.basis: Applicability: code; VBBL 2007 text and 2024 checklists.

metrics.name: Door, corridor and gentle-ramp width per person
metrics.basis: Applicability: code; VBBL 2007 text and 2024 checklists.

metrics.name: Minimum clear stair width
metrics.good: green: each stair >= 1100 and >= required width / number of stairs
metrics.basis: Applicability: code text of VBBL 2007 (3.4.3.2.(7)-(8)); Table 3.4.3.2.-A in BCBC 2024 listed but unread.
metrics.method: size per storey as max(1100, R / n)

metrics.name: Stair width accumulation down the tower
metrics.bad: red: accumulated width used without basis, over-sizing the core
metrics.basis: VBBL 2007 says width need not be cumulative for exits serving floors one above the other, except interconnected floors. Confirm in BCBC 2024 and VBBL 2025.

metrics.name: Travel distance to an exit in a service space
metrics.basis: Applicability: code, 3.4.2.4.(3) and 3.2.1.1.(8); VBBL 2007 text and 2024 checklists.

metrics.name: Travel distance, sprinklered floor area
metrics.basis: Applicability: code, Clause 3.4.2.5.(1)(c); VBBL 2007 text and BCAB 1661 (2009). Re-check the 2024 and 2025 value.

metrics.name: Travel distance, other floor areas
metrics.good: green: <= 40 (business and personal services) or <= 30 (other); preset
metrics.basis: Applicability: code text of VBBL 2007 (3.4.2.5.(1)); 2024 and 2025 values unread. Public-corridor floors up to 105 m under listed conditions.

metrics.name: Rise per stair flight
metrics.basis: Applicability: code, 3.4.6.3; VBBL 2007 text and 2024 checklists.

metrics.name: Exits per floor area
metrics.good: green: >= 2 exits, separation >= half the maximum diagonal
metrics.basis: Applicability: code text of VBBL 2007 (3.4.2.1, 3.4.2.3); 2024 clause numbers confirmed by checklist, values unread.

modules.method: 1) Occupant load per storey = sum of area(use) / factor(use) from an editable Table 3.1.17.1 preset; residential 2 persons per bedroom. 2) Required width R = load x 8, 9.2 or 6.1 mm; with n exits each counted at most R/2, each stair needs at least R/n (n >= 2). 3) Stair clear width = max(1100 mm, R/n), sized per storey and not accumulated, except interconnected floors (3.4.3.2.(6)). 4) Travel distance: rasterise the plate, build a visibility graph (NetworkX) to the nearest exit door, compare with the limit chosen by the sprinkler switch from P11-M09. 5) Stair core area = stairs x width x run plus landings. 6) Report issues to P11-M05. 7) Optional JuPedSim export (P11-M08).

Exit schedule table
modules.human_judgment: Stair strategy (scissor or separate), discharge locations versus active frontage, total versus phased evacuation concept, waiting areas for people who cannot use stairs, fire engineer approval.
modules.limits: Values come from VBBL 2007 text and 2024 checklists; BCBC 2024 and VBBL 2025 tables unread, so presets carry edition stamps. Geometric travel distance ignores furniture and crowd effects. Evacuation time is in P11-M08.

modules.name: Smoke control, stack effect and evacuation simulation (screening)
modules.design_question: Do stack effect, stair smoke control (below and above the lowest exit level) and evacuation flows work in a 250-300 m tower, and how long would stair evacuation take?
modules.effort: L: 15+ person-days (coupling to CONTAM and JuPedSim)
inputs: Layer 0 geometry: storeys, shafts, stairs, doors, below-grade transit-link stairs
Smoke-control strategy and stair classification (above or below lowest exit level) from P11-M05
Stair widths and occupant loads from P11-M06
Climate: January design temperature on a 2.5% basis (Subsection 1.1.3; Vancouver value not retrieved, user entry)

parameters.name: Indoor-outdoor temperature difference and height
parameters.relationship: Stack pressure difference rises with height and temperature difference (dp = g x h x (rho_out - rho_in), ideal-gas density); in cold weather air is pushed into upper floors and shafts, driving smoke spread and door-opening forces.

parameters.name: Below-grade stair smoke control
parameters.relationship: Stairs serving storeys below the lowest exit level, including transit-link levels, must keep contamination to 1% by volume over 2 h; vent or pressurisation area and fan data set whether they do.

parameters.name: Above-grade stair bottom vent
parameters.relationship: Stairs serving storeys above the lowest exit level need a bottom vent of 0.05 m2 per door, at least 1.8 m2; more doors per shaft raise the vent area and ground-level openings.

parameters.name: Occupant load and stair width
parameters.relationship: Higher load per stair width lengthens evacuation time and raises stair density; widths come from P11-M06.

parameters.name: Lift-assisted evacuation
parameters.relationship: Using lifts for assisted or general evacuation shortens total evacuation time of a 250-300 m tower but needs provisions no Canadian clause was found to set; CIBSE Guide D chapter 6.7 covers it.

metrics.name: Contamination in stairs below the lowest exit level over 2 h
metrics.basis: Applicability: code performance requirement 3.2.6.2.(2), BCBC 2018 and VBBL 2007 wording, for stairs below the lowest exit level; re-check VBBL 2025. Earlier 'case target' reading was wrong.

metrics.name: Above-grade stair bottom vent area
metrics.good: green: >= larger of 0.05 x doors and 1.8
metrics.basis: Applicability: code 3.2.6.2.(3); BCBC 2018 (BCAB 1844) and VBBL 2007 agree. Re-check VBBL 2025.

metrics.name: Stack-effect pressure difference across shaft doors (screening)
metrics.good: no sourced limit: report neutral plane and door forces
metrics.basis: Physics gives dp from height and temperature difference; no Canadian door-force limit retrieved here.

metrics.name: Total stair evacuation time
metrics.basis: No Canadian threshold found; report the curve only.

modules.method: Build a multizone airflow network in CONTAM from storeys, shafts and leakage presets; compute stack pressures at the design temperature. Test below-grade stair venting or pressurisation against the 1% over 2 h requirement, and above-grade stairs against the vent rule. Run JuPedSim on the stair geometry with P11-M06 occupant loads for evacuation time and density maps, with and without lift-assisted evacuation. Present all results as screening for the fire engineer. Leakage areas, fan data and walking speeds are editable presets with no sourced values.

modules.limits: CONTAM's graphical interface is Windows-only (engine runs on Linux too). Leakage, fan and walking-speed presets are unsourced. No CFD. Screening for an ideas competition, not an engineering design.

flags.claim: Canadian and Vancouver codes require refuge floors (as in some Asian jurisdictions) in supertall towers.
flags.correction: No refuge-floor clause appears among the 3.2.6 requirements in the 2024 BC Part 3 checklists or the VBBL 2007 text. Treat refuge floors as an alternative-solution option; protected zones (3.3.1.7) are a separate provision.
flags.detail: Evidence: P11-S04, S05, S44. Full-text confirmation against VBBL 2025 and BCBC 2024 is pending because vancouver.ca returned HTTP 403 and the BCBC PDF exceeds the fetch limit.

flags.claim: CIBSE Guide D (2015) provides the current lift-design criteria.
flags.correction: The 2015 edition is superseded by the 2020 edition; the portal now also lists 2025 Guide D items whose status is unconfirmed.
flags.detail: Source P11-S28 (re-opened in r1). Lift criteria here come from papers and standards citing Guide D, so values must be checked against the current edition before submission.

flags.claim: BCBC 2024, with its adaptable-unit rule from 10 March 2025 and the provincial Zero Carbon and Energy Step Codes, is the confirmed governing code for the Vancouver site, and these thresholds are verified.
flags.correction: VBBL 2025 (By-law 14343, in force 15 September 2025, base text BCBC 2024 as amended) governs. Provincial-only rules are shown as reference with Vancouver applicability unverified; Vancouver limits come from VBBL Part 10 and the rezoning policy.
flags.detail: The BC Codes 2024 page says BC Codes do not apply in the City of Vancouver, which has its own building by-law (P11-S01). Vancouver's Part 10 limits were read in VBBL 2019 text (P11-S43). VBBL 2025 text unread.

flags.claim: The 1% contaminated air over 2 h stair target is only a design target from BCAB 1844's facts, not a code limit, and it applies to the tower's exit stairs.
flags.correction: It is a code performance requirement, Sentence 3.2.6.2.(2), for exit stairs serving storeys below the lowest exit level (including transit-link levels), at the January 2.5% design temperature. Stairs above that level get the bottom vent (0.05 m2 per door, minimum 1.8 m2).
flags.detail: Confirmed by BCAB 1844 quoting BCBC 2018 (P11-S09) and by VBBL 2007 text (P11-S44). Re-check numbering in BCBC 2024 and VBBL 2025. P11-M05 and M08 metrics were split by stair location.

flags.claim: RTT = 2H*tv + (S+1)*ts + 2P*tp is the general-analysis form used in P11-S23, and is valid for every rise of a supertall.
flags.correction: P11-S23 prints no such equation. The formula is the classic equal-floor form with no express-jump term and P undefined. The engine uses general analysis with a kinematic express term and P = average car load.
flags.detail: Peters 2000 (P11-S54, abstract only) introduces an express zone term and flight-time formulae; Guide D 2020 text is licensed. Unit tests against the Peters worked example and the Arup rises are required before any gauge shows pass/fail.

flags.claim: No refuge-type provision exists, so any refuge or waiting area is purely a design choice.
flags.correction: Keep 'no mandatory refuge floor'. The 2024 checklists list protected zones in accessible floor areas (3.3.1.7); add it to the checklist (typically met by sprinklers, to confirm in text) plus an evacuation-elevator item.
flags.detail: Evidence: P11-S04 and P11-S05. In VBBL 2007 the article is deleted with a cross-reference to 3.8.3.19 (P11-S48). Operative 2024 and 2025 text unread.

flags.claim: The maximum travel distance for each occupancy is set in 3.4.2.4.
flags.correction: Limit values sit in 3.4.2.5 (location of exits); 3.4.2.4 covers measurement and the 50 m service-space case; 3.3.1.6 covers travel within suites. The sprinkler switch selects the limit.
flags.detail: VBBL 2007 text (P11-S45): 45 m sprinklered, 40 m business and personal services, 30 m other, up to 105 m with a public corridor. BCAB 1661 (P11-S53) confirms 45 m. 2024 and 2025 values unread, so they are unverified presets.

flags.claim: One person per 8 m2 NIA is one of the sourced design densities on an equal footing.
flags.correction: 1 per 8 is a London speculative buffer; the developer expected about 1 per 10 on average. Default office density is 1 per 10 m2 as a team assumption, with 1 per 8 as an option.
flags.detail: Stopes (P11-S22) describes the 1 per 8 figure as a buffer and marketing benchmark.

flags.claim: A 550 kPa plumbing pressure limit forces a plant floor, break tank or reducing station about every 56 m of height.
flags.correction: The 550 kPa limit is handled by PRV stations per domestic-water zone. Plant-floor spacing follows hydronic equipment pressure ratings, air-handling reach and riser congestion (editable presets).
flags.detail: BC Plumbing Code 6.3.3.(1) per BCAB 1454 requires a PRV above 550 kPa (P11-S49); high-rise practice uses PRV stations at zone tops (P11-S52). Plant count is reported as a range.

flags.claim: Passenger-shaft area is the lift core area, so NetToGross computed from it is meaningful.
flags.correction: Total core adds firefighter, stretcher, goods and parking lifts, lobbies, pits and overruns. Passenger-only and total are reported separately and net-to-gross uses the total.
flags.detail: Peters counts passenger shafts only and excludes goods and firefighting lifts and lobbies (P11-S23); 22 Bishopsgate needed a 7,400 kg goods lift (P11-S22).

flags.claim: Residential and hotel lift population can be derived from area / density.
flags.correction: Residential and hotel population uses persons per dwelling by bedroom count or per room with occupancy rate; area-based density applies to offices only.
flags.detail: Arup uses 1.5 to 4.0 persons per unit (P11-S26); UQ uses persons per bedroom (P11-S25). Unit and room counts come from Layer 0 or presets.

flags.claim: BC grid electricity is very low because 0.011 kgCO2e/kWh is its emission factor (and natural gas can be omitted from the factor table).
flags.correction: 0.011 is the Part 9 prescriptive heating-source ceiling for EL-2 to EL-4, not a factor. Electricity and natural gas factors must come from the City Energy Modelling Guidelines; presets are unverified.
flags.detail: P11-S19 states the ceiling and lists only additional fuels; gas and electricity are not in its list. Natural gas is the main fossil fuel in Vancouver Part 3 buildings, so it is added.

flags.claim: VBBL 2025 (By-law 14343, effective 15 September 2025, based on BCBC 2024) is the governing Vancouver by-law, with seismic provisions applying to permits from 15 September 2026.
flags.detail: Effective date 15 Sep 2025 confirmed by a BCIT guide (P11-S50, opened); adoption date, base code and seismic deferral come from unopened City summaries (P11-S12, S13, S14). Sources differ on the Council adoption date.

flags.claim: The 3.2.6.1 triggers (18 m for Groups B and C, 36 m for Groups A, D, E, F, load ratio 300) apply unchanged in BCBC 2024 and VBBL 2025.
flags.detail: BCBC 2024 clause (d), Group C above 18 m, is reproduced in BCAB 1930; NBC original and 2005 commentary give the 36 m rule. VBBL 2007 used 18 m for all groups. Moot at 244-305 m, but the module must show the clause and edition.

flags.claim: Office occupant-load factor of 9.3 m2 per person, a minimum of two exits per floor, occupancy-specific travel-distance limits and 1100 mm minimum stair width apply in current Vancouver code.
flags.detail: Read in VBBL 2007 text (P11-S45, S47): office 9.30, two exits, 30/40/45 m, 1100 mm. Not read in BCBC 2024 or VBBL 2025; the tool carries editable presets with edition stamps.

flags.claim: A 550 kPa static pressure limit applies to plumbing in a Vancouver tower.
flags.detail: 550 kPa requires a PRV under BC Plumbing Code 6.3.3.(1) per BCAB 1454 (1997). Vancouver Book II is NPC 2020-based (P11-S50); text unread. It sets PRV zones, not plant floors.

flags.claim: Destination dispatch cuts trip times by 25% and raises capacity by about 30%.
flags.detail: Appears only as a manufacturer marketing claim cited on a Wikipedia page (P11-S33). Not used as a threshold; simulation must show the benefit.

flags.claim: Stair smoke tenability of at most 1% contaminated air by volume over 2 hours, and stair-bottom vent area of at least 0.05 m2 per door (minimum 1.8 m2), apply in current Vancouver and BC codes.
flags.detail: Superseded in r1: both are code requirements (3.2.6.2.(2) below the lowest exit level; 3.2.6.2.(3) above it) in BCBC 2018 and VBBL 2007. See the FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag on the 1% target. 2024 and 2025 numbering unread.

flags.claim: Firefighter elevator needs 900 kg, 2.2 m2 platform, 60 s run to the top served floor, at most one elevator change and a 1 h shaft-opening closure.
flags.detail: Read in VBBL 2007 Article 3.2.6.5 (P11-S44) only. BCBC 2024 and VBBL 2025 values unread; a City checklist summary also cites a 1 h rating (P11-S15, unopened). Displayed as presets.

flags.claim: Vancouver Part 3 limits are office TEUI 100, TEDI 20, GHGI 3.0; Group C over 6 storeys 120, 30, 3.0; hotel 140, 20, 4.0 kgCO2e/m2a.
flags.detail: From Table 10.2.2.5.A1 of VBBL 2019 consolidated to 27 Feb 2025 (P11-S43). VBBL 2025 Part 10 unread (P11-S61 blocked); a 2022 council report summary says tighter 2025 limits were proposed.

flags.claim: Natural gas emits 0.179 and BC grid electricity 0.011 kgCO2e/kWh in Vancouver compliance modelling.
flags.detail: Recalled from BC practice, not opened. Must be read from the City Energy Modelling Guidelines v3.0 (P11-S58, HTTP 403) before any compliance-style figure is shown.

flags.claim: The tower will be a rezoning, so the Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings and the Higher Buildings Policy apply in addition to the by-law.
flags.detail: Inferred from the VTC brief (9.0 FSR non-residential, 244-305 m). Policy text unread (P11-S57 summary only, HTTP 403).

flags.claim: The below-grade transit link makes the tower a connected building under 3.2.6.3.
flags.detail: Article 3.2.6.3 (Connected Buildings) exists in VBBL 2007 (P11-S44) and is cross-referenced in BCBC 2018 (P11-S09), but is absent from the 2024 checklists. Applicability to the VTC link needs a code consultant.

flags.claim: Plant floors are about 10% of total floors (information range 7 to 26%).
flags.detail: Weak rule of thumb from a tertiary source (P11-S31). Shown as an information range with no pass/fail colouring.

flags.claim: Hotel, cultural, observation and public-use lift criteria; transfers per trip as a design-intent switch; at least two accessible lifts per group.
flags.detail: No sourced figures found. Editable presets; the direct-travel preference comes from a London market expectation (P11-S22), not Vancouver.

flags.claim: Default office density is 1 person per 10 m2 NIA at 80% utilisation.
flags.detail: Chosen because Stopes expected about 1 per 10 on average and treats 1 per 8 as a buffer (P11-S22); UQ uses 1 per 12 (P11-S25). Editable.

flags.claim: Hydronic equipment pressure rating and air-handling reach presets set the plant-floor count range.
flags.detail: No sourced ratings or reach found. Presets are editable and the count is shown as a range.

flags.claim: The tower is sprinklered throughout, and program tags map to occupancy groups as in the preset table (office D, retail E, residential and hotel C, assembly A).
flags.detail: Default in P11-M09; code consultant decides. Group names are consistent with VBBL Part 10 headings (P11-S43).

flags.claim: Transit mode share, station peak flow and escalator capacity are user entries.
flags.detail: No TransLink or CIBSE Guide D escalator figures were sourced; PeakDemandByEntrance uses these entries only.

flags.claim: Numeric Part 3 GHG intensity, TEDI and TEUI limits in VBBL 2025 and the Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings text.
flags.detail: VBBL 2019 Table 10.2.2.5.A1 was read (P11-S43); VBBL 2025 Part 10 and the current rezoning policy were not (HTTP 403). Provincial pages give levels and dates but no numbers.

flags.claim: Firefighter elevator rated load, speed, maximum number of elevator changes and shaft fire rating in BCBC 2024 / VBBL 2025.
flags.detail: Values exist in VBBL 2007 (P11-S44) and archived commentary gives intent only (P11-S06, S08). The operative 2024 and 2025 text must be read from Article 3.2.6.5.

flags.claim: Whether exit-stair width accumulates down the tower in BCBC 2024 / VBBL 2025.
flags.detail: VBBL 2007 3.4.3.2.(4) says width need not be cumulative except at interconnected floors (P11-S45). Confirm in the 2024 and 2025 text; drives stair core area in P11-M06.

flags.claim: Vancouver rules for adaptable dwelling units, power door operators, CSA B651 tactile indicators and accessible hotel rooms in VBBL 2025.
flags.detail: The BC page says BC Codes do not apply in Vancouver (P11-S01). City summaries say accessibility provisions of VBBL 2019 were retained (P11-S12, unopened). Request the City rule.

flags.claim: Seismic, wind-sway, rope-length and stack-effect constraints on lifts in a Vancouver supertall, and Technical Safety BC acceptance of double-deck, multi-car or ropeless lifts.
flags.detail: CSA B44-16 is in force in BC (P11-S51); the page is silent on novel systems. Seismic section details were not opened.

flags.claim: Current BCO Guide to Specification criteria for waiting time and time to destination.
flags.detail: BCO 2014 wording is quoted second-hand by Stopes (P11-S22); later editions were not checked. UK guidance, not a Canadian requirement.

unresolved_relationships: Optimal plant-floor spacing versus tower height: hydronic pressure breaks (equipment rating), floors served per air-handling zone and riser area share of GFA have no sourced relationship or percentage (P11-M03 uses physics for static head, editable presets and an information-only 7-26% range).
Effect of program mix (hotel and residential small risers versus office air shafts) on riser allocation and plant area: not sourced.
